key_insight: Spin-sector dissipation couples spin and orbital angular momentum, with simulations indicating that spin polarization approaches thermal vorticity.
engineering_relevance: Consistent modeling of spin-polarized fluid dynamics requires accounting for antisymmetric stresses in both spin evolution and energy–momentum conservation.
method: Extend perfect spin hydrodynamics with dissipative antisymmetric energy–momentum terms.
Simulate Bjorken flow and boost-invariant, cylindrically symmetric expansion.
evidence_signal: For various kinetic coefficients and relaxation times, simulations in both geometries indicate relaxation toward thermal vorticity, with Israel–Stewart dynamics first approaching the Navier–Stokes regime.
watch_item: Kinetic coefficients and relaxation times remain unspecified a priori, while the Navier–Stokes formulation can introduce higher-than-first-order derivatives that disrupt the equation structure.
paper_title: Novel hydrodynamic features in dissipative spin-polarized fluids
